page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 32 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB per core. Graphics and parallel processing workloads are accelerated by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Notably, this instance does not include local storage, meaning storage must be provisioned externally.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance across multiple domains. Both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng rank in the top 10%, supported by strong single-threaded gzip compression and top-tier bzip3 decompression. Geekbench scores also place the system in the top 10% for single-core and multi-core execution, alongside top-tier image and text processing. However, the Passmark memory score registers in the average tier. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds for small models reach top-tier levels, while medium models perform strongly, and large models drop to average performance tiers.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing a massive 384 GB memory footprint with dual enterprise-grade L40S GPUs, making it a viable alternative to ultra-high-end dedicated GPU clusters for mid-scale workloads. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for sustained, non-burstable CPU-bound tasks, but the hardware profile remains highly optimized for GPU-accelerated workloads. Appropriate workloads include medium-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, database operations, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: The UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a KVM-based, GPU-accelerated server featuring 32 physical AMD EPYC 9575F cores with a shared CPU allocation, 384.0 GB of RAM, and two NVIDIA L40S GPUs providing 96 GB of VRAM. It lacks local storage, requiring external storage configurations. Benchmarks show top-tier CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores in the top 10%, alongside strong memory bandwidth and top-tier database operations. While LLM inference for small and medium models is highly efficient, performance drops to average for large 70B models, and Passmark memory scores remain average. The hardware supports advanced vector and cryptography instructions, enhancing its utility for secure, high-throughput data processing.
